questions.q: What is the difference between a command and an event?
o: A command is a request that can be refused; an event is a fact that already happened
A command is stored forever; an event is deleted after it is handled
A command is published to many listeners; an event has exactly one handler
A command is named in the past tense; an event is named as an order
questions.w: Commands are imperative requests (WithdrawMoney) with one handler and can be rejected. Events are past-tense facts (MoneyWithdrawn), stored forever, with any number of listeners.

questions.q: Two requests load an account at version 3 and both try to append version 4. How does the event store protect the stream?
o: A unique key on (stream, version) lets only one append succeed and the other retries
It locks the whole table until the first request commits
It merges the two events into one and appends it
It overwrites the older event with the newer one
questions.w: Optimistic concurrency: the loser gets a conflict, reloads the stream, runs the rules again and tries version 5. No locks are held while deciding.

questions.q: What is a snapshot in event sourcing?
o: A saved copy of the state at some version that speeds up loading
A backup of the event store taken every night
The only copy of the state once old events are deleted
A read model that is queried by the user interface
questions.w: A snapshot is an optimisation: load it and replay only later events. It can be deleted and rebuilt from the events, which stay the source of truth.

questions.q: Why must a projection be idempotent?
o: Events are delivered at least once, so the same event can arrive twice
Events are always delivered exactly once, but out of order
Read models are never rebuilt after a failure
Projections run inside the command transaction
questions.w: Duplicates and restarts are normal. Store a checkpoint with the update in one transaction and skip positions already applied.

questions.q: A projection has a bug and the balance view is wrong. What is the cleanest fix?
o: Fix the code, reset the checkpoint and replay all events into a fresh read model
Edit the wrong events in the event store
Delete the aggregate and ask customers to reopen accounts
Switch off the read model and read from the old snapshots
questions.w: Events are the source of truth and read models are derived, so a derived view can be dropped and rebuilt by replaying the events.

questions.q: A customer deposits money and the screen still shows the old balance for a moment. What explains this?
o: The read model is updated after the event is stored, so it is eventually consistent
The event store lost the deposit and will retry it
The aggregate rejected the command silently
Snapshots are always one version behind the stream
questions.w: The write side stores the event at once and the projector updates the view slightly later. Use the returned version, an optimistic UI or the aggregate for exact decisions.

questions.q: An event recorded a withdrawal of 200 instead of 20. What should you do?
o: Append a compensating event that reverses it and records the correct amount
Update the stored event to say 20
Delete the event and replay the stream
Ignore it, because events are only a log for debugging
questions.w: Stored events are immutable because others may have used them. A new event corrects the history and shows both the mistake and the fix to auditors.

questions.q: An old event type gained a new required field. How do you let handlers keep seeing only the newest shape?
o: Add an upcaster that converts old versions when events are read
Rewrite every stored event in place during the next release
Reject any event that does not have the new field
Delete the old events and start the stream again
questions.w: Events stay in the store in their original shape. An upcaster converts them to the current version on the way out, so handlers need only one version.
